slides.title: Which of the following are behaviors of active listening? Select all that apply.
text: Question: Which of the following are behaviors of active listening? Select all that apply.
A. Maintaining an open posture.
B. Writing down what the client says so that details are not forgotten.
C. Establishing and maintaining eye contact.
D. Nodding in agreement with the client throughout the conversation.
E. Responding positively when giving feedback.
Correct answers: A. Maintaining an open posture.; C. Establishing and maintaining eye contact.; E. Responding positively when giving feedback.
Topic: Mental Health
notes: Rationale:
Correct:
• “Maintaining an open posture”
• “Establishing and maintaining eye contact”
• “Responding positively when giving feedback”
Not correct:
• “Writing down what the client says so that details are not forgotten” – The nurse should give the client undivided attention.
• “Nodding in agreement with the client throughout the conversation” – The nurse should give quality verbal feedback.
(From your class slides.)

text: Question: Which of the following clients is considered the most at risk for the onset of stress related problems?
A. Client whose father died 3 months ago and lost their job.
B. Client graduating from college and getting married in a month.
C. Client whose new business is growing slowly financially.
D. Client passed over for promotion, who then quit and started their own business.
Correct answer: A. Client whose father died 3 months ago and lost their job.
Topic: Mental Health
notes: Rationale:
Correct: “Client whose father died 3 months ago and lost their job” – They have suffered 2 significant loses.
Not correct:
• “Client graduating from college and getting married in a month” – These are positive events.
• “Client whose new business is growing slowly financially” – This is considered a positive event.
• “Client passed over for promotion, who then quit and started their own…” – Only 1 significant loss.
(From your class slides.)

text: Question: Hospital-based admission has become more oriented to crisis intervention. Which of the following clients have priority for admission to an acute care facility? Select all that apply.
A. Client who lives alone.
B. Client who is acutely psychotic.
C. Client who is depressed.
D. Client who is not sleeping and has a lack of appetite.
E. Client who is dangerous to self and others.
F. Client who is not complying with medication regimens.
Correct answers: B. Client who is acutely psychotic.; E. Client who is dangerous to self and others.
Topic: Mental Health
notes: Rationale:
Correct:
• “Client who is acutely psychotic.” – Yes, safety issues is the admission criteria for mental health clients.
• “Client who is dangerous to self and others.” – Yes, safety issues is the admission criteria for mental health clients.
Not correct:
• “Client who lives alone.” – No, this client is not at a safety risk.
• Client who is acutely depressed No, this client is not at a safety risk.
• “Client who is not sleeping and has a lack of appetite.” – No, this client is not at a safety risk.
• Clients who is not complying with medication regimens No, this client is not at a safety risk.

slides.title: Which of the following foods should the nurse eliminate from the diet of a clien
text: Question: Which of the following foods should the nurse eliminate from the diet of a client experiencing alcohol withdrawal?
A. Milk.
B. Regular coffee.
C. Orange juice.
D. Eggs.
Correct answer: B. Regular coffee.
Topic: Mental Health
notes: Rationale:
Correct: “Regular coffee” – Coffee contains caffeine that increases tremors and agitation.
Not correct:
• “Milk” – Milk is an appropriate choice.
• “Orange juice” – Orange juice is an appropriate choice.
• “Eggs” – Eggs are an appropriate choice.
(From your class slides.)

slides.title: Which of the following clients are at highest risk for suicide completion?
text: Question: Which of the following clients are at highest risk for suicide completion?
A. 85-year-old Caucasian male who lives alone after his wife's death last month.
B. 34-year-old single Hispanic female who recently was diagnosed with cancer.
C. 15-year-old African American female whose boyfriend broke up with her several days ago.
D. 52-year-old Asian male who was terminated from his job because of downsizing.
Correct answer: A. 85-year-old Caucasian male who lives alone after his wife's death last month.
Topic: Mental Health
notes: Rationale:
Correct: “85-year-old Caucasian male who lives alone after his wife's death las…” – Over age 65, male and Caucasian are associated with high suicidal rates.
Not correct:
• “34-year-old single Hispanic female who recently was diagnosed with ca…” – Client is female and Hispanic. Both are associated with low suicidal rates.
• “15-year-old African American female whose boyfriend broke up with her…” – Client is female and African American. Both are associated with low suicidal rates.
• “52-year-old Asian male who was terminated from his job because of dow…” – Although client is male the  Asian culture does not have a high suicidal rate.
(From your class slides.)

text: Question: The nurse is caring for a client with a lithium level of 1.8 mEq/L. The client is due for the next scheduled dose of lithium. Which of the following actions should the nurse perform?
A. Administer the dose of lithium.
B. Hold the dose of lithium.
C. Notify the clients family.
D. Obtain a set of vital signs.
Correct answer: B. Hold the dose of lithium.
Topic: Mental Health
notes: Rationale:
Correct:
• Hold the 5PM dose of lithium. Yes, the level is above 1.5.
Not correct:
• Administer the 5PM dose of lithium. No, the lithium level is above 1.5 so should be held.
• “Notify the clients family.” – No, the lithium level is above 1.5 so should be held.
• “Obtain a set of vital signs.” – No, the lithium level is above 1.5 so should be held.
(Copied from the class slide answer page: live review rn psychosocial integri, slide 35.)

slides.title: The primary health care provider prescribes risperidone for a client with Alzhei
text: Question: The primary health care provider prescribes risperidone for a client with Alzheimer's disease. The nurse anticipates administering this medication to help decrease which of the following behaviors?
A. Sleep disturbances
B. Concomitant depression
C. Agitation and assault potential
D. Confusion and withdrawal
Correct answer: C. Agitation and assault potential
Topic: Mental Health
notes: Rationale:
Correct:
• “Agitation and assault potential” – Yes, antipsychotics are most effective with agitation and assault potential.
Not correct:
• “Sleep disturbances” – No, the medication is an antipsychotic.
• “Concomitant depression” – No, the medication is an antipsychotic.
• “Confusion and withdrawal” – No, the medication is an antipsychotic.
(Copied from the class slide answer page: live review rn psychosocial integri, slide 40.)

slides.title: The nurse is caring for a client with borderline personality disorder. The clien
text: Question: The nurse is caring for a client with borderline personality disorder. The client tells the nurse “you are the best nurse here; the others just want a paycheck.” Which of the following responses by the nurse is appropriate?
A. “Thank you, you are a nice person.”
B. “All of the nurses here provide good care.”
C. “Other clients have told me that also.”
D. “Have you had problems with other nurses?”
Correct answer: B. “All of the nurses here provide good care.”
Topic: Mental Health
notes: Rationale:
Correct: ““All of the nurses here provide good care.”” – This stops the client from ‘splitting’ the nurses.
Not correct:
• ““Thank you, you are a nice person.”” – The nurse needs to understand the client is using splitting behavior and respond with a neutral comment.
• ““Other clients have told me that also.”” – The nurse needs to understand the client is using splitting behavior and respond with a neutral comment.
• ““Have you had problems with other nurses?”” – The nurse needs to understand the client is using splitting behavior and respond with a neutral comment.
(From your class slides.)

slides.title: Which of the following medication amounts is appropriate for a client who is bei
text: Question: Which of the following medication amounts is appropriate for a client who is being treated with imipramine on an outpatient basis for recurring depression and suicidal ideation to have prescribed?
A. 30-day supply
B. 21-day supply
C. 14-day supply
D. 7-day supply
Correct answer: D. 7-day supply
Topic: Mental Health
notes: Rationale:
Correct: “7-day supply” – This medication amount would not allow the client to overdose if taken in its entirety.
Not correct:
• “30-day supply” – This medication is lethal in overdose and the client has suicidal ideation. A 30-day supply would allow them access to potentially overdose.
• “21-day supply” – This medication is lethal in overdose and the client has suicidal ideation. A 21-day supply would allow them access to potentially overdose.
• “14-day supply” – This medication is lethal in overdose and the client has suicidal ideation. A 14-day supply would allow them access to potentially overdose.
(From your class slides.)

slides.title: A paranoid client reports that men in blue clothing keep looking in the window a
text: Question: A paranoid client reports that men in blue clothing keep looking in the window and whispering. Which of the following responses by the nurse is most appropriate?
A. “Those men are groundskeepers. They are talking about their work, not you.”
B. “Do not take things personally, not everyone who is whispering is whispering about you.”
C. “Do not pay attention to the men. Shall we play cards instead.”
D. “I will close the drapes so you can't see the men.”
Correct answer: A. “Those men are groundskeepers. They are talking about their work, not you.”
Topic: Mental Health
notes: Rationale:
Correct: ““Those men are groundskeepers. They are talking about their work, not…” – The nurse does not want to agree with the client. They should be truthful and matter of fact.
Not correct:
• ““Do not take things personally, not everyone who is whispering is whi…” – This disregards the clients thought and appears condescending.
• ““Do not pay attention to the men. Shall we play cards instead.”” – This is distraction and the client will still have the same thoughts.
• ““I will close the drapes so you can't see the men.”” – This does not address the false thoughts of the client.
(From your class slides.)

slides.title: The nurse and unlicensed assistive personnel (UAP) are caring for an agitated cl
text: Question: The nurse and unlicensed assistive personnel (UAP) are caring for an agitated client who had physical restraints applied 5 minutes ago. Which of the following interventions would be appropriate for the nurse to assign to the UAP?
A. Assessing the client’s behavior.
B. Monitoring the client’s orientation level.
C. Providing range-of-motion exercises for the client.
D. Deciding whether or not to remove the client’s restraints.
Correct answer: C. Providing range-of-motion exercises for the client.
Topic: Prioritization & Delegation
notes: Rationale:

UAPs may perform routine, stable tasks such as range of motion and basic care. Assessment, monitoring mental status, and the decision to remove restraints require the RN’s judgment and cannot be delegated.
